definitions.explanation: People who share the same status, characteristic, or situation. Often used as a suffix meaning 'among ~' or '~ with each other'.

examples.japanese: {友達|ともだち}{同士|どうし}で{旅行|りょこう}に{行|い}った。
examples.english: I went on a trip with friends.

examples.japanese: {男|おとこ}{同士|どうし}の{会話|かいわ}だ。
{仲間|なかま}{同士|どうし}で{助|たす}け{合|あ}おう。
examples.english: Let's help each other as comrades.

notes:
USAGE: {同士|どうし} is often used as a suffix attached to nouns to mean 'among ~' or '~ with each other'. It emphasizes shared membership in a group.

COMMON PATTERNS:
・〜{同士|どうし} (among ~, between ~)
・{友達|ともだち}{同士|どうし} (among friends)
・{仲間|なかま}{同士|どうし} (among companions)
・{男|おとこ}/{女|おんな}{同士|どうし} (among men/women)
・{恋人|こいびと}{同士|どうし} (as lovers)
・{親子|おやこ}{同士|どうし} (between parent and child)

HOMOPHONE:
・{動詞|どうし} (verb) - same reading, different meaning

SIMILAR WORDS:
・{仲間|なかま} (companion, colleague)
・{同僚|どうりょう} (colleague at work)
・お{互|たが}い (each other, mutual)
